moved.sentence: When retrieval returns no supporting evidence, the system **SHOULD** abstain ("I don't have enough information") rather than answer from parametric memory.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with its condition (no supporting evidence), the example wording, and the contrast with parametric memory.

moved.sentence: You **MUST** include "unanswerable from context" cases in the eval set and score abstention explicitly — otherwise a model that always answers looks perfect on answerable queries while hallucinating on the rest.
An abstention is a **correct** outcome when context is insufficient; do not penalize it as a miss in aggregate scoring.

judged.note: Abstention as a correct outcome under insufficient context is kept, and the unkeyed do-not-penalize instruction is kept at SHOULD NOT.

moved.sentence: Run groundedness and hallucination evals in CI on a fixed query set; **MUST** fail the build when the hallucination rate regresses past a set threshold.

judged.note: Running the evals in CI on a fixed query set is kept at SHOULD, and the MUST fail-the-build on regression past a threshold is kept at MUST.

moved.sentence: Treat groundedness as a release gate alongside latency and cost, not a one-time benchmark — retriever index drift and model swaps both move it.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the comparison (alongside latency and cost, not a one-time benchmark) and the reason (index drift, model swaps).

moved.sentence: > Privacy note: when eval sets contain user data, redact or synthesize PII before sending to a judge model.

judged.note: The privacy note is kept at SHOULD with its user-data condition and both options (redact or synthesize) before sending to a judge.

moved.sentence: You **MUST** measure groundedness (claim-level support) and a hallucination rate against retrieved sources, and the system **SHOULD** abstain rather than fabricate when support is missing.

judged.note: The MUST on measuring claim-level groundedness and a hallucination rate against retrieved sources, and the SHOULD abstain rather than fabricate, are both kept.

moved.sentence: An LLM judge **MAY** score groundedness by seeing only the answer + retrieved chunks and labeling each claim.
Keep the judge blind to any gold answer so it scores support, not agreement.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the reason: blind to any gold answer so it scores support, not agreement.

moved.sentence: You **MUST** calibrate the judge against a human-labeled gold set and report agreement (e.g., Cohen's kappa) before trusting its scores.

Frameworks such as RAGAS, DeepEval, and TruLens implement these metrics; their absolute scores diverge on the same data (forecast: still true in 2026), so pin one framework + version and track trends rather than comparing raw cross-tool numbers.

judged.note: The framework examples and score divergence (with the 2026 forecast) are kept as the sub-bullet that gives the reason, and pinning one framework + version and tracking trends is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: The system **SHOULD** emit citations to specific source spans (doc id + offset/quote), not just document-level pointers.
You **MUST** verify cited spans rather than trust them: re-check that each quoted span exists in the source and entails the claim.

Score groundedness at **claim granularity**, not whole-answer granularity: decompose the answer into atomic claims and label each `supported` / `partial` / `unsupported` (the FActScore decomposition approach, [arxiv.org/abs/2305.14251](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14251)).

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with claim-level decomposition, the three labels, and the FActScore citation.

moved.sentence: You **MUST** measure retrieval quality (recall@k, context precision) independently — most ungrounded answers trace to missing evidence, not generation, and fixing the generator cannot recover evidence that was never retrieved.
